subject: lunar module
title: What If a Broken Switch Stranded You on the Moon? Apollo 11 Used a Pen

scenes.text: What if one broken switch could strand you on the Moon? On Apollo 11, one nearly did.
July 1969. The moonwalk is over. Back inside the lander, Buzz Aldrin spots something small on the floor.
It's a circuit breaker switch, snapped off the panel, probably by a backpack. It's the breaker that powers the ascent engine, their way off the Moon.
They report it and try to sleep. By morning, Houston still has no fix.
Aldrin won't put a finger or anything metal into a live circuit. He pushes a felt-tip pen into the hole.
The breaker holds. The engine fires. Decades later, the pen and the broken switch sold at auction for 857,600 dollars.

description:
What if a snapped switch kept you from leaving the Moon? After the Apollo 11 moonwalk in July 1969, Buzz Aldrin found the engine-arm circuit breaker switch broken off on the cabin floor, probably knocked by a backpack. It was the breaker that sent power to the ascent engine.
Mission Control had no fix by morning. Aldrin pushed a felt-tip pen into the opening rather than a finger or anything metal, and the breaker held. The pen and the switch later sold at Sotheby's for 857,600 dollars.
